nodes.summary: Let $\mathrm{SB}(\alpha)$ be the Stern–Brocot representation of a real number $\alpha$, let $Q$ be Hida's map from sequences over $\{L, R\}$ to sequences over $\{O_L, E_R, O_R, E_L\}$, and let $I$ be the set of admissible sequences over $\{O_L, E_R, O_R, E_L\}$. Then $Q$ maps the set of Stern–Brocot representations $\{\mathrm{SB}(\alpha) : \alpha \in (0, 1) \text{ irrational}\}$ bijectively onto $I$: for every…
nodes.title: Hida's map $Q$ is a bijection onto $I$

nodes.summary: Let $I$ be the set of admissible sequences over $\{O_L, E_R, O_R, E_L\}$, let $T$ be Hida's map from sequences over $\{O_L, E_R, O_R, E_L\}$ to sequences over $\{L, M, R\}$, and let $M(\alpha)$ be the Mallows representation of a real number $\alpha$. Then $T$ maps $I$ bijectively onto the set $\{M(\alpha) : \alpha \in (0, 1) \text{ irrational}\}$: for every $x \in I$ the sequence $T(x)$ lies in this set, $T$ is…
nodes.title: Hida's map $T$ is a bijection from $I$ onto the Mallows representations

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$ be irrational, let $x = \mathrm{SB}(\alpha)$ be its Stern–Brocot representation, let $q = Q(x)$ be the image of $x$ under Hida's map $Q$ to sequences over $\{O_L, E_R, O_R, E_L\}$, and let $T(q)$ be the image of $q$ under Hida's map $T$ to sequences over $\{L, M, R\}$; all sequences are indexed from $0$. Let $o(i)$ be the $i$-th position, counting from $0$, at which $q$ takes the value $O_L$…
nodes.title: Block-matching lemma

nodes.summary: The constant sequence whose every term is $O_L$ does not belong to the set $I$ of admissible sequences over $\{O_L, E_R, O_R, E_L\}$.
nodes.title: The constant sequence $O_L O_L O_L \cdots$ is not admissible

nodes.summary: With fractions encoded as pairs (numerator, denominator) of natural numbers, the mediant of the gap bounded by $0/1$ and $1/1$ is $1/2$, that is, the pair $(1, 2)$.
nodes.title: The mediant of $0/1$ and $1/1$

nodes.summary: For a gap bounded by two fractions $n_1/m_1$ and $n_2/m_2$, each encoded as the pair (numerator, denominator) of natural numbers, the mediant is the fraction $(n_1 + n_2)/(m_1 + m_2)$, encoded as the pair $(n_1 + n_2, m_1 + m_2)$.
nodes.title: Mediant of a gap

nodes.summary: A sequence over $\{L, M, R\}$ is the Mallows representation $M(\alpha)$ of some irrational $\alpha \in (0, 1)$ if and only if it is neither eventually constantly $L$ nor eventually constantly $R$.
nodes.title: Characterization of Mallows representations

nodes.summary: A sequence over $\{L, R\}$ is the Stern–Brocot representation $\mathrm{SB}(\alpha)$ of some irrational $\alpha \in (0, 1)$ if and only if it is neither eventually constantly $L$ nor eventually constantly $R$.
nodes.title: Characterization of Stern–Brocot representations

nodes.summary: For every irrational $\alpha \in (0, 1)$, the Mallows representation $M(\alpha)$ is eventually periodic if and only if $\alpha$ is a real quadratic irrational, that is, algebraic of degree $2$ over $\mathbb{Q}$.
nodes.title: Lagrange's theorem for Mallows representations

nodes.summary: For every irrational $\alpha \in (0, 1)$, the Mallows representation $M(\alpha)$ is eventually periodic if and only if the Stern–Brocot representation $\mathrm{SB}(\alpha)$ is eventually periodic.
nodes.title: Mallows and Stern–Brocot representations are eventually periodic together

nodes.summary: For every set $A$ and every $c \in A$, the constant sequence $(c, c, c, \dots)$ is positively Poisson stable.
nodes.title: Constant sequences are positively Poisson stable

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$ be irrational, with continued fraction expansion $\alpha = [0; a_1, a_2, \dots]$. Then the Mallows representation of $\alpha$ is positively Poisson stable if and only if the sequence $(a_1, a_2, \dots)$ of its partial quotients is positively Poisson stable.
nodes.title: Poisson stability of the Mallows representation and the continued fraction

nodes.summary: For every irrational $\alpha \in (0, 1)$, the Mallows representation of $\alpha$ is positively Poisson stable if and only if the Stern–Brocot representation of $\alpha$ is positively Poisson stable.
nodes.title: Poisson stability of the Mallows and Stern–Brocot representations

nodes.summary: A sequence $x = (x_0, x_1, x_2, \dots)$ with values in a set $A$ is positively Poisson stable if there is an index $n_0$ such that for every length $\ell$ there is a shift $p \ge 1$ with $x_{n_0 + p + t} = x_{n_0 + t}$ for all $t < \ell$; that is, every initial block of the tail $(x_{n_0}, x_{n_0 + 1}, \dots)$ occurs again at a later position.
nodes.title: Positively Poisson stable sequence

nodes.summary: The set $I$ consists of the infinite sequences $x = (x_0, x_1, \dots)$ over the alphabet $\{O_L, E_R, O_R, E_L\}$ such that $x_0 = O_L$; no two consecutive terms $(x_j, x_{j+1})$ form one of the pairs $(O_L, O_R)$, $(O_L, E_L)$, $(E_R, E_L)$, $(E_R, E_R)$, $(O_R, O_L)$, $(O_R, E_R)$, $(E_L, E_L)$, $(E_L, E_R)$; $x$ is not eventually constant equal to $O_L$, nor eventually constant equal to $O_R$; and no tail of $x$…
nodes.title: The admissible parity sequences $I$

nodes.summary: Let a vertex of the Mallows tree have gap $(a, b)$, where $a$ and $b$ are fractions, and let $\langle p, q \rangle$ be the pair of fractions that Mallows' insertion rule inserts between $a$ and $b$. The left, middle and right children of the vertex have gaps $(a, p)$, $(p, q)$ and $(q, b)$ respectively.
nodes.title: Children of a Mallows-tree vertex

nodes.summary: Let a vertex of the Mallows tree have gap $(a, b)$ and label $\langle p, q \rangle$, the pair of fractions that Mallows' insertion rule inserts between $a$ and $b$. For a real number $\alpha$, the letter chosen at this vertex is $L$ if $\alpha < p$; otherwise it is $M$ if $\alpha < q$, and $R$ if $\alpha \ge q$.
nodes.title: Letter chosen at a Mallows-tree vertex

nodes.summary: Mallows' insertion rule inserts the pair $\langle 4/7, 3/5 \rangle$ between the fractions $1/2$ and $2/3$ (here the left fraction $1/2$ has odd numerator).
nodes.title: Mallows insertion between $1/2$ and $2/3$

nodes.summary: Mallows' insertion rule inserts the pair $\langle 1/2, 2/3 \rangle$ between the fractions $0/1$ and $1/1$, so the first level of the Mallows tree is $MT_1 = \langle 1/2, 2/3 \rangle$.
nodes.title: Mallows insertion between $0/1$ and $1/1$

nodes.summary: Let $n_1/m_1$ and $n_2/m_2$ be fractions, given as pairs of natural numbers (numerator, denominator). Mallows' insertion rule inserts between them the ordered pair of fractions $\langle (n_1 + n_2)/(m_1 + m_2),\ (n_1 + 2n_2)/(m_1 + 2m_2) \rangle$ if $n_1$ is even, and $\langle (2n_1 + n_2)/(2m_1 + m_2),\ (n_1 + n_2)/(m_1 + m_2) \rangle$ if $n_1$ is odd. The rule is applied to adjacent fractions $n_1/m_1 < n_2/m_2$.
nodes.title: Mallows' insertion rule

nodes.summary: Fractions $n/m$ are written as pairs $(n, m)$ of natural numbers. For a list of fractions $a_0, a_1, \dots, a_k$, this is the list obtained by taking, for $j = 0, 1, \dots, k - 1$ in turn, the two fractions $p_j, q_j$ (in this order) that Mallows' insertion rule inserts between $a_j$ and $a_{j+1}$, that is, the list $p_0, q_0, p_1, q_1, \dots, p_{k-1}, q_{k-1}$. It is empty when the list has fewer than two entries.
nodes.title: Fractions inserted by one Mallows step

nodes.summary: Fractions $n/m$ are written as pairs $(n, m)$ of natural numbers. For a gap $(a, b)$ let $\langle p, q\rangle$ be the pair that Mallows' insertion rule inserts in $(a, b)$. For a real number $\alpha$, the gaps $I_0, I_1, \dots$ are defined by $I_0 = (0/1, 1/1)$ and, if $I_i = (a, b)$, by $I_{i+1} = (a, p)$ when $\alpha < p$, $I_{i+1} = (p, q)$ when $p \le \alpha < q$, and $I_{i+1} = (q, b)$ when $\alpha \ge q$. In…
nodes.title: Gaps along the Mallows path of a real number

nodes.summary: In the Mallows tree, the root is labelled $\langle 1/2, 2/3\rangle$, its middle child is labelled $\langle 4/7, 3/5\rangle$ and its right child is labelled $\langle 3/4, 4/5\rangle$.
nodes.title: Labels of the first Mallows-tree vertices

nodes.summary: For a word $w$ over the letters $L$, $M$, $R$, the label of the Mallows-tree vertex reached from the root by the path $w$ is the pair $\langle p, q\rangle$ of fractions that Mallows' insertion rule inserts in the gap $(a, b)$ of that vertex.
nodes.title: Labels of the Mallows tree

nodes.summary: The letters of Mallows representations are the three distinct letters $L$, $M$ and $R$, standing for "left", "middle" and "right".
nodes.title: The Mallows alphabet

nodes.summary: Encode each vertex of the Stern–Brocot tree (left subtree, root $1/2$) by its gap, so that the root is the gap $(0/1, 1/1)$, and extend $\psi_{\mathrm{SBT}}$ and $\varphi_{\mathrm{SBT}}$ to lists of vertices by applying them to each entry and concatenating the results in order. Then for every $i \ge 1$ the ordered list $MT_i$ of fractions inserted at step $i$ of Mallows' construction is…
nodes.title: Mallows levels from the Stern–Brocot maps

nodes.summary: The ordered list of fractions inserted at the second step of Mallows' construction is $MT_2 = \langle 1/3, 2/5, 4/7, 3/5, 3/4, 4/5\rangle$.
nodes.title: The second Mallows level

nodes.summary: Fractions $n/m$ are written as pairs $(n, m)$ of natural numbers. Start from the list $\langle 0/1, 1/1\rangle$ and refine it repeatedly, each refinement step inserting between every two adjacent entries the pair of fractions given by Mallows' insertion rule. For $i \ge 1$, $MT_i$ is the list of the fractions inserted at the $i$-th step: the fractions that Mallows' rule inserts between adjacent entries of the list…
nodes.title: Mallows levels

nodes.summary: Fractions $n/m$ are written as pairs $(n, m)$ of natural numbers. The root of the Mallows tree has gap $(0/1, 1/1)$. If a vertex has gap $(a, b)$ and Mallows' insertion rule inserts $\langle p, q\rangle$ in $(a, b)$, then its children along the letters $L$, $M$ and $R$ have gaps $(a, p)$, $(p, q)$ and $(q, b)$. The node of a word $w$ over $L$, $M$, $R$ is the gap of the vertex reached from the root by following the…
nodes.title: Gaps of the Mallows tree

nodes.summary: Let $x = x_0 x_1 x_2 \cdots$ be a sequence in the admissible set $I$ over the letters $O_L$, $E_R$, $O_R$, $E_L$, and for $i \ge 0$ let $p_i$ be the $i$-th position (counting from $0$) at which $x$ has one of the letters $O_L$, $O_R$. Then for every $i \ge 0$, $p_{i+1} > p_i + 1$ holds if and only if $p_{i+1} = p_i + 2$.
nodes.title: Gaps between odd letters of admissible sequences

nodes.summary: Let $x = x_0 x_1 x_2 \cdots$ be an infinite sequence over the parity alphabet $\{O_L, E_R, O_R, E_L\}$ with $x_0 = O_L$, and call a position $j \ge 0$ odd when $x_j \in \{O_L, O_R\}$. Then the $0$-th odd position of $x$, the smallest odd position, is $0$.
nodes.title: The first odd position of a sequence starting with $O_L$

nodes.summary: Let $x = x_0 x_1 x_2 \cdots$ be an infinite sequence over the parity alphabet $\{O_L, E_R, O_R, E_L\}$, and call a position $j \ge 0$ odd when $x_j \in \{O_L, O_R\}$. For $i \ge 0$, the $i$-th odd position of $x$ is the $(i+1)$-st smallest odd position of $x$, and it is $0$ by convention when $x$ has at most $i$ odd positions.
nodes.title: Odd positions of a parity sequence

nodes.summary: The parity alphabet consists of the four letters $O_L$, $E_R$, $O_R$ and $E_L$. The intermediate set $I$ linking the Stern–Brocot and Mallows representations is a set of infinite sequences over this alphabet.
nodes.title: The parity alphabet

nodes.summary: Let $x = x_0 x_1 x_2 \cdots$ be an infinite word over $\{L, R\}$ with $x_0 = R$ and $x_1 = L$. Then the parity sequence $Q(x) = Q_0 Q_1 Q_2 \cdots$ of $x$ satisfies $Q_0 = O_L$, $Q_1 = E_R$ and $Q_2 = O_R$.
nodes.title: First values of the parity sequence

nodes.summary: Let $x = x_0 x_1 x_2 \cdots$ be an infinite word over $\{L, R\}$. Its parity sequence $Q(x) = Q_0 Q_1 Q_2 \cdots$ over the parity alphabet $\{O_L, E_R, O_R, E_L\}$ is defined by $Q_0 = O_L$ and $Q_{j+1} = \mathrm{step}(Q_j, x_j)$ for every $j \ge 0$, where $\mathrm{step}$ is the transition rule of the parity sequence.
nodes.title: The parity sequence of a Stern–Brocot word

nodes.summary: The map $\mathrm{step}$ sends a letter of the parity alphabet $\{O_L, E_R, O_R, E_L\}$ and a letter of $\{L, R\}$ to a letter of the parity alphabet, by $\mathrm{step}(O_L, L) = O_L$, $\mathrm{step}(O_L, R) = E_R$, $\mathrm{step}(E_R, L) = O_R$, $\mathrm{step}(E_R, R) = O_L$, $\mathrm{step}(O_R, L) = E_L$, $\mathrm{step}(O_R, R) = O_R$, $\mathrm{step}(E_L, L) = O_R$ and $\mathrm{step}(E_L, R) = O_L$.
nodes.title: Transition rule of the parity sequence

nodes.summary: Let $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_k$ be a finite list of fractions, each fraction $n/m$ recorded as the pair $(n, m)$ of natural numbers. Its refinement is the list obtained by keeping every entry and inserting, between each two consecutive entries $a_t$ and $a_{t+1}$, the two fractions that Mallows' insertion rule places between them, in the order the rule gives them. A list with fewer than two entries is its own refinement.
nodes.title: One refinement step of the Mallows tree

nodes.summary: For almost every irrational $\alpha \in (0, 1)$, with respect to Lebesgue measure, the factor complexity of the Mallows representation $M(\alpha)$ satisfies $p_{M(\alpha)}(n) = 3^n$ for every $n \ge 0$.
nodes.title: Factor complexity of almost every Mallows representation

nodes.summary: Let $w$ be a finite word over $\{L, M, R\}$ that contains the letter $M$ or contains both $L$ and $R$. Then for almost every irrational $\alpha \in (0, 1)$, with respect to Lebesgue measure, $w$ has frequency $0$ in the Mallows representation $M(\alpha) = M_0(\alpha) M_1(\alpha) M_2(\alpha) \cdots$: if $N_n$ is the number of positions $i < n$ with $M_i(\alpha) M_{i+1}(\alpha) \cdots M_{i+|w|-1}(\alpha) = w$, then…
nodes.title: Words of frequency zero in almost every Mallows representation

nodes.summary: For almost every irrational $\alpha \in (0, 1)$, with respect to Lebesgue measure, the Mallows representation $M(\alpha) = M_0(\alpha) M_1(\alpha) M_2(\alpha) \cdots$ satisfies, for every $\ell \ge 0$,
nodes.title: Matching fractions of almost every Mallows representation

nodes.summary: For Lebesgue-almost every $\alpha \in (0, 1)$, if $\alpha$ is irrational, then there is a finite word $w$ over $\{L, M, R\}$ that does not occur relatively densely in the Mallows representation $M(\alpha) = M_1(\alpha) M_2(\alpha) \cdots$: there is no $\ell > 0$ such that, for every $i \ge 0$, the window $M_{i+1}(\alpha) \cdots M_{i+\ell}(\alpha)$ contains an occurrence of $w$.
nodes.title: Words without bounded gaps in almost every Mallows representation

nodes.summary: Each of the following holds for Lebesgue-almost every $\alpha \in (0, 1)$, provided $\alpha$ is irrational: (i) the Mallows representation $M(\alpha)$ is not eventually periodic; (ii) $M(\alpha)$ is positively Poisson stable; (iii) $M(\alpha)$ is transitive, that is, every finite word over $\{L, M, R\}$ occurs in $M(\alpha)$.
nodes.title: Typical properties of Mallows representations

nodes.summary: Let $\ell \ge 0$. For a word $w = w_1 \cdots w_\ell$ over $\{L, M, R\}$, let $C_w$ be the set of irrational $\alpha \in (0, 1)$ whose Mallows representation begins with $w$, that is, $M_t(\alpha) = w_t$ for $1 \le t \le \ell$. nodes.summary: For every $i \ge 1$, the set of irrational $\alpha \in (0, 1)$ whose Mallows representation has $i$-th letter $M_i(\alpha) = M$ has Lebesgue measure less than $3 - 2\sqrt{2}$.
nodes.title: Measure bound for the letter $M$ at a fixed position

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$ be irrational, with continued fraction expansion $\alpha = [0; a_1, a_2, \ldots]$. The letter $L$ does not occur in the Mallows representation $M(\alpha)$ if and only if $a_1 = 1$, $a_2$ is odd, and the sequence $a_3, a_4, \ldots$ is a concatenation of blocks, each of the form $(2, b)$ or $(1, c, 1, b)$ with $b$ even. nodes.summary: Let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$ be irrational, with continued fraction expansion $\alpha = [0; a_1, a_2, \ldots]$. The letter $M$ does not occur in the Mallows representation $M(\alpha)$ if and only if $a_{2k}$ is even for every $k \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Mallows representations without the letter $M$

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$ be irrational, with continued fraction expansion $\alpha = [0; a_1, a_2, \ldots]$. The letter $R$ does not occur in the Mallows representation $M(\alpha)$ if and only if $a_2 = 1$, $a_3$ is even, and the sequence $a_4, a_5, \ldots$ is a concatenation of blocks, each of the form $(2, b)$ or $(1, c, 1, b)$ with $b$ even. nodes.title: Mallows representations without the letter $R$

nodes.summary: For every real number $\alpha < 1/2$, the first letter $M_1(\alpha)$ of the Mallows representation of $\alpha$ is $L$.
nodes.title: The first Mallows letter below one half

nodes.summary: For a real number $\alpha$, the Mallows representation $M(\alpha) = M_1(\alpha) M_2(\alpha) \cdots$ is the infinite word over $\{L, M, R\}$ that records the path of $\alpha$ down the Mallows tree. nodes.title: The letter $M$ in $T(Q(\mathrm{SB}(\alpha)))$ marks the ends of runs

nodes.summary: For a truth value $b$ and letters $a, a'$ of $\{O_L, E_R, O_R, E_L\}$, the letter $\tau(b, a, a') \in \{L, M, R\}$ is defined as follows. If $b$ is true, it is $L$ when $a = O_L$ and $R$ otherwise. If $b$ is false, it is $M$ when $a \ne a'$, $L$ when $a = a' = O_R$, and $R$ when $a = a' \ne O_R$.
nodes.title: The letter rule of $T$

nodes.title: The pair $(1, 2)$ encodes $1/2$

The child of a gap $(a, b)$ in direction $L$ is the gap $(a, a \oplus b)$, and its child in direction $R$ is the gap $(a \oplus b, b)$. nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a real number and let $(a, b)$ be a gap with fractions $a = n_1/m_1$ and $b = n_2/m_2$ (pairs of natural numbers). The letter chosen at $(a, b)$ is $L$ if $\alpha$ is less than the real number $(n_1 + n_2)/(m_1 + m_2)$, the value of the mediant of $a$ and $b$ (the label of the Stern–Brocot vertex with this gap), and $R$ otherwise.
nodes.title: The Stern–Brocot choice at a vertex

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$ be irrational and let $f_1(\alpha), f_2(\alpha), \dots$ be the fractions on its Stern–Brocot path. Then there are no natural numbers $c$ and $j_0$ such that the numerator of $f_j(\alpha)$ has remainder $c$ modulo $2$ for all $j \ge j_0$: the parities of these numerators are not eventually constant.

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$ be irrational with continued fraction expansion $\alpha = [0; a_1, a_2, \ldots]$. The Mallows representation of $\alpha$ is transitive, that is, every finite word over $\{L, M, R\}$ occurs in it as a factor, if and only if every finite word over the positive integers occurs as a factor of the sequence $a_1 a_2 a_3 \cdots$.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
